Fontlex Relaxed Math

The box below is a plain text box holding math the way people type it in plain text: (a+b)/(c+d), x^2, sqrt(x). The font typesets it as you type: fractions, roots, superscripts and subscripts, laid out by the text engine that lays out the letters. Ordinary text stays ordinary, so and/or, w/o, dates and paths are left alone. The characters stay exactly as typed. No script on this page lays anything out.

Each line is read on its own. A construct that isn't complete yet, or that breaks a rule below, stays as its characters until it is. Inside a fraction the caret stays at the fraction's start: the fraction's glyphs are drawn where they belong, but take no room of their own.

What it typesets

  • Fractions: 1/2, x/2, 2a/3, (a+b)/(c+d), f(x)/2, 1/(1+1/x). Parentheses around a whole part go; with a script after them they stay: (a+b)^2/c.
  • Scripts: x^2, x^(n+1), x^-1, x_1, H_2O, and both at once, stacked: x_i^2.
  • Roots: sqrt(x^2+1).
  • Symbols: <= >= != -> => +- become ≤ ≥ ≠ → ⇒ ±. Greek letters and other symbols can be typed as themselves, but Chrome shapes Greek and Latin letters apart, so there a construct that mixes them (e^(iπ)) stays as its characters.
  • Constructs inside constructs, 3 deep, with at most 2 fractions inside one another, and at most 24 characters in a construct that isn't inside another.

What stays text

  • A fraction's parts are numbers (12, 3.5), a number and a letter (2a), one letter, a group in parentheses, a call like f(x) or sin(x), or a root, each with its scripts. Longer words make no fraction: and/or, km/h, page/2.
  • Two lone letters make a fraction only in an expression (a+b/c, x = a/b), so w/o, n/a and I/O stay as they are.
  • Slashes in a row (a/b/c, 10/23/2026, //) make none, nor does any slash in a run of characters where one touches a longer word (tr/a-z/A-Z/).
  • No script touches another underscore, and a number has no subscript: file_1_2, 1_000 stay text.
  • A space inside a construct leaves it as its characters: write (a+b)/2, not (a + b)/2.

How it works

122 passes read each line the way the rules above say, and rewrite it as the LaTeX that lays out the same: (a+b)/(c+d) as \frac{a+b}{c+d}, with the parentheses as its braces and a \frac and braces that the line doesn't have inserted as glyphs that draw nothing. Then Fontlex Math's own passes lay it out. The font has 55,176 glyphs and 2,044 substitution and 301 positioning lookups.

Results

Each line is shaped with the font, what it draws is read back from the glyphs (characters by name and size, rules from their outlines), and compared with a separate Python model of the notation (relaxed.py), to the font unit.
